subject: Post-demo: Model fit & safety follow-ups / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 20:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Model fit & safety follow-ups / next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our side: 

- Recap of discovery: HealthScope is evaluating a clinical triage assistant to surface relevant intake recommendations and flag high-risk cases. Main constraints: 200ms median token latency target for triage flow, strict refusal behavior on PHI/diagnosis requests, and audit trails for model decisions.
- We committed to: 1) a short model-fit evaluation with recommended model variants, 2) a prompt set that captures common triage asks and sensitive edge cases, and 3) an initial safety/refusal matrix for review.

Attached: redwood_eval_summary.pdf (high-level results), prompt_set_v1.csv (30 sample prompts including sensitive cases), safety_refusal_matrix.xlsx (initial pass on refusal behaviors).

Our recommended model candidates based on the call: 
- redwood-llama-70b-q4f (best latency/cost balance for your throughput)
- redwood-ggml-13b-8k (lower-cost option with stronger safety tuning in our tests)
- redwood-instruct-70b (if you need higher long-form rationale and auditability)

Benchmarks: short summary page at https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/healthscope-2026 — contains token-level latency distributions and quality evals vs. your sample data.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm which prompts we should prioritize from the prompt_set_v1.csv (3-5 to start).
2) We run a focused model-fit eval on those prompts and share a detailed rubric + signal-level diffs (ROUGE/Exact/Refusal rate).
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rishi to review safety failure cases and mitigation options.

Any timeline preferences on your side? We can have the first eval back within 3 business days once prompts are selected.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198


---

On Tue, 3 Mar 2026 at 19:02 Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthscope.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo earlier — Emily
>
> A couple of quick clarifications: 1) for refusal behavior we need explicit policy alignment when patients ask for diagnostic advice (we should refuse + give next steps), and 2) auditability: we need contextual traces linking output to prompts for compliance.
>
> Also looping in Alex from procurement for timeline/PO questions.

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@healthscope.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & safety follow-ups / next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the attachments. A few things from our side: 

- We reviewed the sample prompts and prioritized 5 to start (I've highlighted them in the attached prompt_set_v1.csv and added two high-risk variants).
- Timeline: procurement would like an initial eval within 4 business days to align budget planning.
- Safety requirements: 
  * Must refuse direct diagnostic instructions and provide a standardized escalation message.
  * Maintain a per-interaction trace (prompt + model response + model id + timestamp) exportable as JSON (for audit ingest).

Can you confirm whether the redwood-llama-70b-q4f evaluation will include the refusal tests out-of-the-box, or is that additional safety tuning?

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Product Lead, Patient Intake
HealthScope
emily.zhang@healthscope.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & safety follow-ups / next steps

Hi Emily —

Perfect — thanks for prioritizing the prompts. Quick answers and plan: 

- Refusal testing: our eval harness will run the prioritized prompts against the three candidate model variants and compute a refusal_rate metric based on our safety classifier and heuristic checks. For cases where the model did not refuse appropriately, we'll include suggested guardrail prompts and prompt-engineering patterns (e.g., system-level refusal templates and instruction scaffolding). This is included in the scope of the initial eval.

- Audit traces: we can produce per-interaction JSON exports (prompt, response, model_id, timestamp, confidence proxies) and deliver a sample export with the eval results. We'll mark that as a deliverable in the report.

- Timeline: we'll run the focused eval and aim to deliver by Mon, 9 Mar 2026 (within your 4-business-day window). If that works we'll proceed once you confirm the final prompt picks.

Attachments included in this email: redwood_eval_summary.pdf, prompt_set_v1.csv, safety_refusal_matrix.xlsx

Next internal step: Rishi (cc'd) will lead the safety analysis and flag any regression risks vs. your baseline. Monica will coordinate the deliverable packaging and HubSpot deal updates.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & safety follow-ups / next steps

Quick internal notes (sharing here so thread metadata stays with customer):

- Action: I'll run the safety/refusal suite first against redwood-llama-70b-q4f and redwood-ggml-13b-8k. If we see >5% unexpected acceptance on high-risk prompts, escalate to instruction fine-tuning simulation.
- Regression concern: the customer indicated they want auditability and stricter refusals vs. their current baseline (legacy rule-based). Historically, moving to more powerful models increases 'creative' refusals in unconstrained prompts; we'll track refusal_quality (binary) and refusal_consistency (across paraphrases).
- Deliverable checklist for Monica to attach: 
  * eval_results.csv (per-prompt per-model signals)
  * refusal_cases.md (annotated failures)
  * export_sample.json (audit trace example)

I'll aim to get a first pass by Mon morning PST. If we need additional safety tuning, we'll scope a short eng/ops ticket (estimate 3-5 days) and note cost implications.

-Rishi
Senior Applied ML, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
